text:
Matt: Quick sync — we need to pick a collector topology for per-tenant TTLs and retention across traces/metrics/logs. sidecar vs gateway? tradeoffs for cost, QoS, and rollouts.
Dina: TLDR: sidecar = tenant isolation + local sampling but higher infra overhead. gateway = central control + easier per-tenant retention, but risk of hotspots/backpressure. :thinking_face:
Xavier: Agree. Also consider head vs tail sampling location. If we do tail-based sampling at the gateway we need full trace reassembly + buffering -> memory pressure and longer latency.
Priya: For retention we want 3 classes: hot (7d), warm (30d), cold (archive). Customers want per-tenant overrides. Gateway makes policy enforcement simpler.
Matt: Are we comfortable with gateway re-batching losing span timestamps/ordering? That's been a support headache before.
Dina: We can preserve timestamps if gateway avoids rewriting spans. But re-batching will change chunk boundaries; some downstream exporters assume per-request ordering.
Xavier: Another concern: billing and cost estimation. If we proxy everything through gateway, egress costs concentrate and make per-tenant cost attribution harder unless we attach token metadata early.
Priya: We can stamp tenant_id in Resource attributes at the agent (sidecar) so gateway and exporters can attribute without deep inspection.
Matt: Quick config sketch for OTEL collector (idea):
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  batch:
exporters:
  otlp/http:
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp/http]
``` 
Dina: If we run that in the gateway and enable tail-sampling, add `memory_limiter` and `tail_sampling` processors. But memory_limiter needs tuning per-tenant.
Xavier: Could do hybrid: sidecar does head-sampling and quick drops for noisy clients, gateway does policy and tail-sampling for important tenants. That reduces gateway burden while keeping control.
Priya: UX question: Console rollout should expose 'simulated retention cost' for a pipeline config before applying. Engineers want a quick estimate: tokens/s, avg span size, projected monthly GB.
Matt: +1. Also a canary path: route X% of tenant traffic to new gateway pipeline to validate tail-sampling correctness.
Dina: On exporters: chaining vs parallel. We have customers asking for primary exporter + cold-archive exporter. OTEL supports multiple exporters, but we should be careful about retries — independent retry loops can duplicate traffic on failure.
Xavier: For retries I'd prefer a durable queue between processors and exporters, with exactly-once being hard — at least implement idempotency keys in archive writes.
Priya: Retention TTL enforcement: do it at the gateway for cold tier and on sidecars for local disk-based retention. Sidecar-based local buffering for intermittent connectivity is useful.
Matt: What about per-signal pipelines? I.e., separate pipelines for traces, metrics, logs — should each tenant get independent retention settings?
Dina: Yes. Signals have different cardinality and storage costs. Make UI allow per-signal overrides and sensible defaults.
Xavier: Operational impact: if we have per-tenant pipelines in the gateway, config explosion is real. Consider templated pipeline definitions with tenant variables substituted at runtime.
Priya: Also need to think about quotas + backpressure. If a tenant exceeds ingestion quota, gateway should return HTTP 429 to agent which can then shed lower-priority data.
Matt: For load-shedding we should support priority attributes on spans (e.g., sampling.priority) and simple token-bucket quotas per-tenant.
Dina: Monitoring: dashboards should surface gateway memory pressure, tail-sampler queue depth per-tenant, requeued spans, and exporter latency. Add alerts for >70% mem and queue depth spikes.
Xavier: Security: gateway does tenant auth and mTLS to exporters. Sidecars authenticate to gateway with short-lived tokens minted by our control plane.
Priya: Action items:
- (Matt) Prototype hybrid flow: head-sample sidecar + gateway tail-sample for 2 tenants. (ETA 2w)
- (Dina) Add console cost estimator mockups for pipelines. (ETA 1w)
- (Xavier) Design memory_limiter + queue sizing defaults and doc. (ETA 1w)
- (Priya) Define tenant stamping and auth flow for sidecar->gateway tokens. (ETA 3 days)
telemetry-bot: created incident ticket TLM-423 for gateway memory testing.
Matt: Cool. If no objections I'll start the prototype tomorrow. Feel free to drop comments inline or push mocks to the Figma link: https://redwood.design/telemetry-pipeline-mock
Priya: +1 from me. :thumbsup:
Dina: +1 — will pair on sampling tests.
Xavier: +1 — will add exporter idempotency checklist to the doc.
Matt: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after initial prototypes.
